title: 3'-Seq
scope: The single Illumina 3′-Seq schematic for detecting 3′-UTR isoforms, interpreted at the bead-bound, uridine-primed nick-translation implementation described by Lianoglou et al. (2013). The far-left highlighted transcript is an explanatory target icon, followed by one linear material route through reverse transcription, second-strand synthesis, RNase HII nicking, nick translation, blunting, and PCR/purification to a cDNA library. The primary-caption-supported second-adapter interface is explicitly identified as text-resolved. No alternate workflow is depicted. Associated kit names, reviews, and application papers do not expand the method scope. Adapter ends are identified by their primer-borne versus blunt-ligated roles because the drawing does not label P5/P7.

states.label: Poly(A)-ended RNA primed on a magnetic bead
features: The RNA substrate is drawn purple with an A-rich tail. The separate far-left yellow-highlighted 3′ region and label “3′-Seq to detect 3′ UTR isoforms” identify the biological target, rather than a second workflow branch.
The depicted NVTTTUTT(T)n primer contains a VN anchor and a single ribouridine (red U) within oligo(dT). The catalogue defines V as dA, dC, or dG.

The primer carries a 5′ sequencing-adapter segment and biotin attached to a streptavidin-coated magnetic bead. The RNA/primer complex is the starting interface; attachment and annealing are already represented, without separate operation captions.
The reported starting sample is total RNA; the pictured priming interaction represents a poly(A)-ended RNA within it.

The first cDNA strand is generated by reverse-transcribing total RNA using an oligo(dT) primer containing a VN-anchor (where V is dA, dC, or dG), P5 adapter sequence, a uridine, and biotin that is bound to a streptavidin-coated magnetic bead.

Total RNA was reverse-transcribed with an oligo(dT) primer extended at the 5′ end by a sequencing adapter bound to magnetic beads. The oligo(dT) primer contained a uridine. After second strand synthesis, a nick was introduced at the uridine, and nick translation was used to shift the nick ∼50–75 nt away from the 3′ end. At the new position of the nick, a blunt end was created, and the second sequencing adapter was ligated.

method_scopes.rationale: All six captioned transformations belong to the single 3′-Seq route. The additional ligation interface o5a is resolved from primary Figure 1A and the matching catalogue description, rather than claimed as a separately drawn panel. The checked collection page is headed “3’-Seq: Quantitatively Measure Abundance of 3’UTR Isoforms” and captions its drawing “A schematic overview of 3’-seq.” This establishes its match to the assigned card. The scope is this supported implementation, not all methods that sequence transcript 3′ ends.
